scope: the per-entity payload: one changed-bit at 1329, which in our body is 1 - so the client takes the struct-copy branch instead of the delta decoder

the_payload_loop_0x471de3.0x471DE3: index derived from the frame clock; edi = &entityRing[i] with stride 0x34 (52 bytes)
the_payload_loop_0x471de3.0x471E03: call 0x447190 -> READ 1 BIT (the per-entity changed flag)
the_payload_loop_0x471de3.0x471E0E: if the bit is 1: read N bits (N = [ebp+8], the id width) and copy 13 dwords (52 bytes) into the entity ring slot
the_payload_loop_0x471de3.0x471E4A: if the bit is 0: call 0x671700 - the per-entity DELTA decoder
the_payload_loop_0x471de3.0x471E59: test eax,eax ; jne 0x471DDA - loop for the next entity

the_delta_decoder_0x671700.0x671722: read 1 bit; if 1 -> read 2 bits, mode = value + 1
the_delta_decoder_0x671700.0x67173F: read 1 bit; if 1 -> read 2 bits, mode = value + 5
the_delta_decoder_0x671700.0x67175B: a third branch reads another bit
the_delta_decoder_0x671700.interpretation: the delta payload begins with a variable-length selector that chooses a delta MODE

what_our_body_actually_has.consequence: the changed flag is 1, so the client reads N bits and copies a struct instead of decoding a delta - which is not what a fresh entity should do, and is a plausible cause of the exit

the_next_experiment: clear bit 1329 to 0 so the changed flag is 0 and the delta decoder 0x671700 runs
then observe whether the client survives the snapshot and what mode the selector picks from the following bits
